summary: Retest of AI Writing Coach frontend fixes from iteration_24. HIGH apply-fix corruption bug is FIXED: with only the last docs block edited ('i dont like it'), Submit (gate ON) hard-halted, 'Apply all fixes' changed ONLY that block to "I don't like it" while block1 stayed exactly 'My First Document' and block2 untouched; resubmit then graded (F, tasks incomplete) with no re-halt. MEDIUM over-highlight bug is FIXED: 'Check my writing' produced exactly 2 .hq-squiggly spans ('i','dont') scoped to the edited block — no underlines inside 'First'/'Click'. Email flow (email-m3) verified: compose squigglies (3), send -> Submit hard-halt with 6 issues, per-issue Apply fix correctly rewrote the sent body ('hello ms rivera' -> 'Hello Ms. Rivera'), sent reading pane showed 2 remaining squigglies. Guide gate toggle (writing-gate-toggle) toggled ON->OFF instantly, did NOT flip back after 3s (stale-GET race gone) and persisted across reload; red flag writing-flag-em-exp-docs visible in Reports. Gate OFF let the explorer submit dirty writing (grade dialog + 'Submitted with 2 unresolved writing issues' toast). Backend pytest test_writing_coach.py: 15/15 after clearing leftover seed data (see minor note).

minor.issue: Not a product bug: test_resubmit_clean_clears_flag initially failed because writing_flag is aggregated per TRACK (any mission with unresolved_writing>0) and the iteration_24 seed left docs-m2 unresolved_writing=6. After zeroing docs-m2 the test passes; suite is 15/15. Consider making the test self-contained (clear other missions of the track first).

issues: Still open from iteration_24 (informational): the checker proofreads seeded starter blocks too, so a student can be halted by curriculum text they never typed (did not reproduce a halt from starter text in this run — seeded docs-m1 text is clean).

critical_code_review_comments: Fixes look correct: StudioMission.proofreadDoc proofreads per block and tags blockId; applyIssueToDoc only mutates the block whose id === issue.blockId using findBoundaryIndex-based replaceOnce; DocEditorCore filters issues by blockId. No further changes needed for these two defects.

Overlapping LLM issues (e.g. 'hello ms rivera', 'ms rivera', 'hello ms rivera i') mean after applying one fix the overlapping siblings silently no-op / their squigglies disappear. That is the documented safe behavior, but 'Apply all fixes' can therefore leave nested duplicates unresolved (student may need a second pass). Optional improvement: dedupe/merge overlapping issue ranges before showing them.
applyFix still drops issues by object identity (arr.filter(i => i !== issue)); works but a stable id would be safer (carried over from iteration_24).

success_rate.frontend: 100% of retested flows (apply-fix targeting, squiggly boundaries, docs check, email halt/apply, gate toggle persistence, gate-OFF submit + red flag)

seed_data_creation: Deleted em-exp's email-m3 draft to get a clean compose (recreated by the test send). Restored guide em-guide writing_gate = true (ON). Left studio_progress em-exp/docs-m2 unresolved_writing=6 so the red 'Writing issues' flag in Guide Reports stays reproducible; docs-m1 unresolved_writing=0.
test_credentials: Explorer em-exp/em_exp_tok, Guide em-guide/em_guide_tok, Fresh em-fresh/em_fresh_tok (cookie session_token httpOnly/secure/sameSite None or Bearer)
context_for_next_testing_agent: Writing Coach is now green end-to-end. Repro used: cookie-inject em_exp_tok on https://explorer-journey-4.preview.emergentagent.com -> /studio/docs/docs-m1, fill last textarea[data-testid^='studio-block-'] with 'i dont like it', studio-submit-btn -> studio-writing-halt-note -> writing-apply-all-btn. Guide: /guide -> Reports tab -> writing-gate-toggle (remember to leave it ON). Backend pytest suite must have only one docs mission flagged per track when asserting writing_flag clearing. Also noted a pre-existing React hydration console warning from the injected instrumentation wrapper inside <option> in DocEditorCore's line-spacing select (dev-tooling only, harmless).
rca_of_the_issue: Previous root cause (joined-document proofread losing per-block offsets) is resolved by per-block proofreading + blockId-scoped, word-boundary single-occurrence replacement. The one backend test failure this run was stale seed data (docs-m2 unresolved_writing=6) making the track-level writing_flag stay true, not an API defect.
